title: Reading the markers

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: The merge is still paused. Git wrote both versions into index.html.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Run `git status` to see which file needs you. Git calls it "both modified".

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Then `cat index.html` to read it. You will see three strange lines.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Between `<<<<<<<` and `=======` is **your** version, the branch you are on.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Between `=======` and `>>>>>>>` is **their** version, the branch coming in.

story.speaker: Ada
story.text: Those marker lines are not code. They are notes from git, and they must all go.

items.text: Answer: what happens to the marker lines?

questions.prompt: You are on main. Which version sits between <<<<<<< and =======?

choices.text: Sam's "Riverside Lantern Festival", because main is where I am

questions.explanation: The top half is always the branch you are standing on. You are on main, so the top half is main's version.

questions.prompt: What should you do with the <<<<<<<, ======= and >>>>>>> lines?

choices.text: Delete all of them while choosing what the file should say

questions.explanation: They are temporary notes. If you leave them in, they end up in your real file as broken text.

recap: In a conflict, the top half (after <<<<<<<) is the branch you are on and the bottom half is the branch coming in. All three marker lines must be deleted.
hints: Ask git which file needs attention, then read that file.
`git status` names the conflicted file. `cat <file>` prints it so you can see the markers.
Run `git status`, then `cat index.html`, then answer both questions.
